translation.title: Diclofenac Diethylamine Gel
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for pain relief and anti-inflammation in traumatic inflammation of tendons, ligaments, muscles and joints (sprains, bruises, etc.), localized forms of soft-tissue rheumatic diseases (tenosynovitis, shoulder-hand syndrome, bursitis, periarthritis, etc.), and localized forms of rheumatic diseases (osteoarthrosis of the peripheral joints and spine, etc.).
translation.usage: Adults and adolescents 12 years and older: apply 2 to 4 g at a time to the affected area 3 to 4 times a day according to the size of the painful area, and rub in gently.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are or have been hypersensitive to it, if you have experienced hypersensitivity such as asthma attacks, hives or acute rhinitis to aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, for children 12 years and under, or if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Consult a doctor or pharmacist before use if you have bronchial asthma, if you are elderly, or if you are or have been hypersensitive to propylene glycol. Do not use it on damaged skin (hemorrhagic skin diseases, eczema, infected lesions, burns, wounds), in the eyes, or on mucous membranes. Wash your hands after use unless treating the finger joints. Do not use it under an occlusive dressing. Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are taking loop diuretics (furosemide, etc.), thiazide diuretics, medicines that interfere with hemostasis (warfarin, etc.), antiplatelet agents (aspirin, etc.), selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors or serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors. Adverse reactions may occur - sometimes rash, eczema, erythema (red patches) and dermatitis (including contact dermatitis); temporary irritation and tingling on damaged skin; systemic reactions with long-term use over large areas; rarely bullous dermatitis, and very rarely hypersensitivity, angioneurotic edema (swelling), asthma, photosensitivity and pustular rash; and serious skin reactions such as exfoliative dermatitis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, or serious gastrointestinal reactions including bleeding, ulcer and perforation of the stomach or intestine; if any of these occur, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Store below 30 degrees Celsius.
